Run a HAI prioritisation exercise for local context

Feed surveillance results back to frontline, clinical leads and management

Introduce IPC bundles and checklists

Audit waste management practice
Develop guidelines for SSI, CLABSI, HAP, CAUTI, MDR, disinfection, HCW safety, antibiotic stewardship
Train staff on new/updated guidelines
Run regular IPC training for health care workers
Run regular IPC training for cleaners and support staff
Create link nurse / IPC champion network
Train administrators and managers in IPC
Train surveillance staff; standardise data collection and quality review
Start surveillance for SSI, device-associated and MDR infections
Audit catheter care, wound dressing, isolation and ward cleaning
Use surveillance data to plan unit-level improvements and review AMR
Introduce daily signed cleaning records
Allocate a dedicated IPC budget
Appoint a full-time IPC professional
Assess staffing (WISN), maintain agreed ratios, act on shortfalls
Meet ward design and >1 m bed-spacing standards; respond to over-capacity
Secure reliable water, drinking-water stations and wastewater treatment
Secure continuous power, PPE, supplies and sterile-equipment availability
Make laboratory support and IT for surveillance reliable
